_comment: Consumer release binding for the remote Memory MCP transport (ADR-0053, CANONICAL_LAW §8.10).
Read by ops/memory_remote/bridge.py. An 'admitted' release is accepted only after three checks:
(1) exact identity: semver version, full 40-hex source_sha, tag v<version>, the version's wheel name, full 64-hex wheel_sha256;
(2) consistency with authenticated evidence: it must be the very release the consumer's governed pin proves
(ops/config/memory-binding.json, rebuilt from source by memory-cross-repo.yml, and the uv.lock published wheel hash);
(3) admission authenticity: admission_receipt is a structured l9.receipt/admission@1 reference for this exact subject,
and an ADMITTED verifier for that receipt type must exist. None exists today, so the hosted transport stays refused
(BLOCKED, by design) even for a fully consistent binding.
Values the live service reports (memory.capabilities) are self-reported and checked only for drift, never as release evidence.
candidate names release-candidate bytes the consumer may be qualified against on loopback only, under an explicit
L9_MEMORY_REMOTE_CANDIDATE_QUALIFICATION reason. It never reaches a hosted endpoint and is never an admission.
No endpoint, credential, grant or key belongs in this file: the endpoint is operator-supplied per machine.
